summary: Iteration 4 full-stack testing of 6 new modules (Messages, Support, Founder Office, Website Builder, Client Portal, Documents rich-text). Backend: 29/29 pytest pass after fixing Message.sender_id required->Optional bug. Frontend: all critical flows verified end-to-end with 0 failed API responses.
critical_code_review_comments: Recurring anti-pattern (3rd time now in iters 1/3/4): DB Pydantic model has a required field (Message.sender_id) that the endpoint auto-assigns from current_user *after* validation, causing 422 when frontend omits it. Fixed by making sender_id Optional. Long-term fix: introduce dedicated *CreateRequest schemas (e.g. MessageCreate) so DB required fields do not leak into API validation surface. Suggest sweep of remaining models (Client.contact_person? Employee.user_id? etc.) for the same pattern.

server.py is now ~1176 lines and hosts ~70 endpoints in a single module. Above the 700-line threshold - recommend splitting into routers/ per domain (messages, support, founder, website, client_portal).

GET /api/client-portal/overview: returns ALL org projects/invoices/tickets to every authenticated user (comment even acknowledges 'For MVP: show all... In production: filter by client_id linked to user'). This is a data-leak risk when non-owner clients log in - a client would see other clients' data. Should filter by client_id or user_id linked to that client.

POST /api/strategy and GET /api/strategy require role in ['owner','admin'] - reasonable, but PUT/DELETE for strategy items are not implemented at all (can create but never edit or delete). Consider adding update/delete or documenting as intentional.

publish_website endpoint (PUT /api/websites/{id}/publish) does not check ownership - any authenticated user in any org can publish any website by ID (only relies on obscurity of website_id). Same for update_page. Add org/owner filter to update_one query.
WebPage.slug is not validated to be unique per website - two 'Home' pages with slug='home' can be created for the same website.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (added TestMessages, TestSupport, TestFounderOffice, TestWebsiteBuilder, TestClientPortal - 8 new tests)

success_rate.frontend: 100% for all iter-4 flows (Messages channel+send, Support ticket create+manage+save, KB article create, Founder overview+strategy+checklist toggle+AI insights 849 chars from GPT-5.2, Website builder create+edit+save+publish, Client portal stats, Documents rich-text toolbar). 0 failed API responses captured on network.

seed_data_creation: Test data with TEST_ prefix created via both pytest and playwright: channels, messages, tickets, kb-articles, strategy items, checklist items, websites, documents. No cleanup performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent:
Iter-4 fully green. Only change made: models.Message.sender_id Optional (same class of bug as iter1 owner_id and iter3 organizer_id). Frontend correctly reads user.user_id for rendering sender bubble alignment. AI Insight endpoint (via /api/ai/message with GPT-5.2 through EMERGENT_LLM_KEY) returns high-quality strategic advice in ~8s. Website builder auto-creates a home page on website create - editor pre-populated with '

Welcome to your new website

'. Rich text editor is contentEditable-based with a working toolbar (Bold/Italic/Underline/H1/H2/Quote/Code/UL/OL/Link buttons all render).
rca of the issue: POST /api/messages failed with 422 'Field required: sender_id' because models.Message.sender_id was declared as required 'str'. The endpoint sets msg_data.sender_id = user.user_id INSIDE the handler, but Pydantic validation runs first on the incoming JSON which never contains sender_id (frontend Messages.js only sends channel_id, content, message_type). Fix: made sender_id Optional[str] = None. Verified via pytest (TestMessages passed) and playwright (message sent + rendered with correct sender bubble).
